generation.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: one cohesive five-tool pixel-art spritesheet for the existing Mirror Island cozy farming game.
Primary request: redesign the five basic farming tools as a clear, attractive, consistent set in the project's chosen fresh pastoral style. These will be reduced to small inventory icons and held by a tiny game character, so readability is more important than decorative detail.
Canvas: landscape 1536 by 1024 pixels, a precise invisible grid of 3 columns and 2 rows, each cell 512 by 512. Genuinely transparent background with alpha, including the watering can handle holes. Do not draw checkerboard squares, a backdrop, ground shadows, panels, borders, grid lines, text, labels, numbers, watermarks, hands, characters or plants.
Layout, fixed order: top-left a farmer's HOE with one broad rectangular perpendicular steel blade on a long oak handle; top-middle a MINT GREEN WATERING CAN with a real open arch handle, compact rounded body and spout pointing upper-right ending in a clearly perforated round rose; top-right a single-bladed AXE with a broad steel wedge and pale oak handle. Bottom-left a PICKAXE with two opposing narrow curved steel points and a long oak handle; bottom-middle a SHORT SICKLE with one recognizably curved crescent blade and a short oak handle. Bottom-right completely empty and transparent. Exactly one object in each of the five occupied cells.
Composition: consistent diagonal orientation of handled tools, grip at lower-left and working head at upper-right. Each object centered within its own cell with at least 64 pixels empty padding. Match apparent visual weight across tools, no object crossing a cell boundary. Keep the hoe head visibly different from both the axe and the pickaxe. The sickle must have a big clear crescent opening, not resemble a pickaxe.
Style: authentic deliberately simple low-resolution game pixel art, chunky clean stepped pixel clusters, as if each cell was drawn on a strict 32 by 32 logical pixel grid and enlarged using nearest neighbor 16 times. Square solid pixels, no antialiasing, no subpixel slivers, no noisy microtexture, no smooth gradients, no illustration brushwork, no 3D rendering. Crisp silhouettes with a restrained one-logical-pixel dark muted teal outline. Simple two or three shade material ramps and broad readable highlights.
Palette and materials: all four wooden handles use the same pale warm oak, honey highlight and cinnamon shadow. All five steel surfaces use the same pale silver, icy mint highlights and desaturated blue teal shade. Watering can mint enamel, warm cream highlight and blue teal base, a small warm oak grip. Limit the entire set to roughly 14 harmonious solid colors. One consistent light source from upper-left. Pleasant spring mood, practical ordinary starter tools, no ornate trim, no badges, no gems, no faces.
Output must be an actual isolated spritesheet with alpha, not a presentation board.

alphaAttempt.prompt:
Use case: background-extraction
Edit target: the provided five-tool Mirror Island spritesheet.
Make exactly one correction: remove the entire white and light gray checkerboard background and return a PNG with actual transparent alpha (alpha 0 for background), not a drawing that imitates transparency. Remove the checkerboard from both open watering-can handle gaps and around the sickle's crescent.
Preserve every tool's silhouette, colors, wooden handle, mint enamel, steel shading, pixel edge, scale, location, and all spacing. Preserve the canvas at 1536 by 1024, the existing 3-column by 2-row layout, and the empty bottom-right cell. Keep all tool pixels opaque. Do not add or redraw any objects, drop shadows, panel, text, or any opaque background color. Only replace background pixels with genuine transparency.
